'''''Eutrochium purpureum''''', commonly known as '''sweet Joe Pye weed''',<ref>[https://illinoispollinators.org/plant/sweet-joe-pye-weed/ "Sweet Joe Pye Weed"] at Illinois Pollinators website. University of Illinois Extension. 2023. Retrieved 25 December 2025.</ref> '''sweet-scented Joe Pye weed'''<ref name=USDA/> or '''purple Joe Pye weed''',<ref name=gobotany/> is an herbaceous [[perennial plant]] in the family [[Asteraceae]]. It is native to eastern and central [[North America]], from [[Ontario]] east to [[New Hampshire]] and south as far as [[Florida]], [[Louisiana]], and [[Oklahoma]].<ref name=BONAP/>

==Description==
''Eutrochium purpureum'' is a clump-forming herb that grows to {{convert|1.5|–|2.4|m|ft|sp=us}} tall and about {{convert|1.2|m|ft|abbr=off|sp=us}} wide. Plants are found in full sun to part shade in mesic to wet soils. [[Plant stem|Stem]]s are upright, thick, round, and purple, with [[Whorl (botany)|whorls]] of leaves at each node. As the plant begins to bloom the stems often bend downward under the weight of the flowers. The leaves grow to {{convert|30|cm|in|abbr=on}} long and have a somewhat wrinkled texture. The purplish flowers are produced in large loose, convex shaped compound corymbiform arrays. Plants bloom mid to late summer and attract much activity from insects that feed on the nectar produced by the flowers.

==Taxonomy==
''Eutrochium purpureum'' shows a high amount of variability, and up to two or three varieties are currently recognized by current botanical authorities. They differ based in leaf shape, leaf pubescence, and achene glandularity. The precise delineation of these varieties is difficult due to integration between them. The commonly recognized varieties are:<ref name=weakley2020/><ref name=Sorrie/>
*''Eutrochium purpureum'' var. ''carolinianum'' – Southeastern [[Piedmont (United States)|Piedmont]]
*''Eutrochium purpureum'' var. ''holzingeri'' – Midwestern U.S.
*''Eutrochium purpureum'' var. ''purpureum'' – Widespread in eastern North America

This species [[Hybrid (biology)|hybridizes]] readily with other species of ''[[Eutrochium]]'' and where this species and those species overlap in distribution the resulting plants can be difficult to resolve to a specific [[taxon]].<ref name=FNA/>

==Ecology==
Many species of butterflies, moths, bees, and flies visit the flowers.<ref name=fotcr2017/>

It is larval host to the [[eupatorium borer moth]] (''Carmenta bassiformis''), the [[red groundling moth]] (''Perigea xanthioides''), the [[Phragmatobia fuliginosa|ruby tiger moth]] (''Phragmatobia fuliginosa''), and the [[Schinia trifascia|three-lined flower moth]] (''Schinia trifascia'').<ref name=Xerces/>

The larvae of ''[[Calycomyza flavinotum]]'', a [[leaf miner]] fly, create blotch-shaped mines on the leaves.<ref name=fotcr2017/>

==Cultivation==
{{Also|Eutrochium#Uses}}
Like other Joe Pye weed (''Eutrochium'') species, ''Eutrochium purpureum'' is cultivated as an ornamental landscape plant,<ref name="Botanica 359"/><ref name="Hawke"/> and has escaped from cultivation in parts of New Zealand.<ref name="fnz-genus"/>  ''E. purpureum'' and ''[[Eutrochium maculatum|E. maculatum]]'' (spotted Joe Pye weed) are sometimes confused with each other or treated interchangeably in the gardening world due to their similar appearance.<ref name="Hawke"/>
